body.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathfrak M_T^{\mathrm{low}}(\alpha,\beta,L,c,\varepsilon)\), the deterministic lower-envelope quotas and the interval \(I_{T,\Delta}\) are uniformly honest and have expected length at most a constant multiple of \(r_{T,\Delta}\).
body.justification: This convenience corollary extracts the constructive upper half of \texttt{thm:one-sided-minimax-length-frontier}. Together with that theorem's same-class converse, it shows that a one-sided rare-arm floor plus a control-arm floor yields the exact class-minimax expected-length order, without a rare-arm upper envelope.
body.gap: Shi, Wang, and Wu use one-sided forced exploration for delayed asymptotic inference under outcome--delay independence. This corollary records that the same design-side floor, together with the explicit control floor, supports the rate-optimal honest construction under unrestricted within-arm outcome--delay dependence; the matching lower bound is already supplied by \texttt{thm:one-sided-minimax-length-frontier}.
body.consumer: Analysts whose logs certify the rare-arm forced-exploration floor and the control-arm floor may use the interval with the exact worst-case class-minimax rate interpretation. A policy that allocates the rare arm more often may improve policy-specific performance or exact constants, but not the minimax order over the full one-sided class.
